rationale: This is a mechanical mashup of two archive signals — the round-trip MIN conjunction and the industry-z-scored dilution/liquidity pair — with only a dvc→dvc+prstkc substitution, so it tests no new economic mechanism and mostly re-prices the same firms already ranked by both parents.

target_name: Peer-abnormal issuance episodes under thin liquidity
rationale: This is a parameterization variant of the archive's "Serial-issuer frequency under thin liquidity" — swapping a 2% absolute dilution threshold for a 0.5 industry-z threshold and z-scoring the liquidity leg — which is a cosmetic robustness check rather than a distinct hypothesis, and the arbitrary-cutoff objection is not resolved, only relocated.

target_name: Peer-relative payout rigidity under thin liquidity
rationale: It is literally the archive's "Committed payout mix with thin liquidity" with IND_ZSCORE wrapped on both legs, so despite a genuinely clean diagnostic purpose (is the −6.8% alpha sector composition or firm choice?) it re-proposes an evaluated signal and, on already-thin 6.5% coverage, industry demeaning risks reducing it to noise.

The working-capital productivity gap is a genuinely different conditioning construct than the che/lct level the archive has leaned on six times, but both legs are close to established anomalies (share issuance, working-capital accruals/asset growth) and the unwinsorized raw growth difference inside RANK invites outlier-driven ordering in small-denominator firms.

target_name: Peer-relative dilution against deteriorating cash coverage
rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archive's "Equity proceeds that fail to build cash" (dilution rank minus the change in cash coverage) with the deflator changed from at to lct plus industry z-scoring, and the two legs are mechanically linked — an equity raise directly increases che — so the "stock vs flow" question is confounded by the issuance itself rather than isolated.

target_name: All funding taps open under weak obligation coverage
rationale: The MIN conjunction of equity and short-term-creditor draw is a structurally distinct mechanism from the additive stack, and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the base pair (dilution vs oancf/lct) already produced a dead alpha in the archive and the lct-growth leg overlaps heavily with the known asset-growth/net-operating-liability anomaly, so the incremental content is modest.
